value: Same-Goal saved correction lets the owner change the requirement of queued, waiting, paused or running local work without replacing the Goal. It does not give back consumed model or step allowance, and it never silently adopts output produced for the superseded requirement. Old Brief, grant, questions, artifacts, verifications and receipts remain inspectable as superseded history. The latest pause/cancel intent and the latest-prior grant ceiling carry forward. A slow old callback keeps the single slot until it ceases, so old and new revisions never execute concurrently. This serves the SPEC requirements 'Corrections supersede older information' and 'Late results from stale revisions/epochs are rejected', and the D-021 Stable-1 outcome that correction acts on the intended work. The value is structural only so far. In Root's demo, one Goal reaches revision 2 completion with cumulative model 2 / step 1 usage, and the late old compose output is never saved. However, the correction is declared by a trusted host fixture rather than interpreted from natural language. User-perceived value therefore awaits PRI routing and the human usefulness evaluation, and it is not claimed here.
responsibilities: In the inspected excerpts, the separation is consistent with PAL-contracts-v5 section 2. TSK owns Brief and Condition IDs, revision/epoch/state, grant intersection, question status, lease/call/reservation/Step cessation validation and the change notice (tasks_v5.py _change 980-1035, _old_calls 1037-1090, release 1163-1228). TSK performs no meaning inference. It checks stored target and revision, strict shape, the repository grant (_intersect of the host grant and the latest prior grant) and same-transaction source availability through _gate. MEM owns the saved correction record and the source gate. ART and VER are unchanged and fence old writes through revision/epoch (Root connection tests for ART-save and VER-save commit order). RUN is unchanged: MockRunner.release forwards the TSK result without comparing the reply WorkRef to the captured one, and yield_or_retain leaves fencing to TSK (mock_runner_v5.py run_once). The direct INSERT into v5_intake_event inside _change (around 1028-1031) is the frozen Root pre-mint choice inside TaskStore's own writer, not a cross-owner write. One obligation has no implemented owner yet: provenance. The trusted host must list every reused or derived record in context_refs. Only a deterministic fixture currently does this, and PRI (C01) is unimplemented. No role assumes another owner's authority.
contract_alignment: CHANGE01/1 and C10: control keeps the closed command (_obj with kind, brief and origin_record_ref; origin kind must be record). The _transaction replay lookup runs before operation(), so an identical replay returns the original receipt before any authority check (114-128, 1092-1161). _change follows the frozen order: (1) latest/stale check via _current(epoch=False); (2) terminal conflict; (3) state domain; (4) _questions; (5) flag type check; (6) running if and only if a lease exists, and an older lease requires drain; (7) origin-reuse conflict; (8) grant/target denied; (9) _gate on origin plus explicit context; (10) MAX overflow; (11) guarded Condition and event mints (_change_mint savepoint with total_changes and in_transaction guard, 962-978). All of these run before the first owned write. A single transaction then inserts revision+1/epoch+1 with the same goal, session and expert, marks the old row superseded, clears the old flags, supersedes only open questions, sets new flags (carried pause, drain=1) for running or (0,0) otherwise, and appends one 'work changed' state event with refs [origin]. Grant never refunds: _remaining (185-192) reads Goal usage, so consumed amounts above narrower limits leave zero headroom. C02: get_work overlays only open questions, so superseded history reports empty open_questions; the demo history shows state superseded. C13: claim selects only latest-revision queued rows (237-263), and retained old leases fail _authority (149-159). Cross-revision release requires the old row to be superseded and the latest row to be running+drain or cancelled. It runs _old_calls before any write, abandons only old started Steps, and settles in the order cancel, then pause, then queued, so an old failed outcome cannot fail the replacement. The b4baae24 repair is visible in _old_calls: shared _id parsing for call, reservation and optional Step; a call id equal to the C15 canonical identity; and required <= call sources <= registered. C14: one event per change, in the same transaction. Source stop: invalidate_by_refs (1230-1274) acts only on latest revisions, matching SCOPE 'Source-stop ordering correction'. Abnormal-case proof is attributed, not executed by this reviewer. Root connection tests (tests/test_change_connection_v5.py) cover admit, finish, ART save, VER save, complete, answer and source-stop commit orders plus the change write lock. Root's integrity regression and the independent Sol linked-ID probe cover consistently corrupted identities. No divergence was found between the inspected code and the frozen scope.

Omitted methods were not inspected, and no coverage is inferred for them. They include _questions, _intersect, _mint, _event, _claim_wire, _register, _check_sources, admit_call/end_call/get_call, create/answer/complete, IntakeStore, the MEM/ART/VER/READ owners and the contracts_v5 parsers. Fixed TSK, RUN and integrity test files other than tests/test_change_connection_v5.py were not supplied. This reviewer executed no tests, demo, probe or commands. The following are Root evidence: full845 PASS (26.939 s, exit 0), the 51 new methods, the actual demo, the connection tests, the integrity regression and the exact byte/hash checks. The following are the independent Sol reviewer's evidence: the original REQUEST_CHANGES reproduction, the 51 focused and 122 related runs, and the linked-ID probe results (original mutation; now unavailable with mutated=False). Nothing here claims a real provider, UI, service or external effect; PRI natural-language or semantic authority; semantic usefulness; general restart recovery; old or live DB migration; or whole-PAL or product acceptance. findings: No blocking finding in the inspected CHANGE01/1 design or excerpts. F1, medium (a forward dependency, not a CHANGE01 defect): if the process crashes while any lease is active, the single slot stays permanently blocked. This applies especially to a CHANGE cross-revision draining lease or an admitted call. The evidence: claim rejects a different runner with conflict (tasks_v5.py 243-245); MockRunner mints a fresh runner_id per process (mock_runner_v5.py module docstring and MockRunner.__init__); an admitted call cannot be dispatched again and makes release return conflict; and OWNER-EXCERPTS states that TaskStore has no recover method. SCOPE excludes general restart recovery, so this is correctly out of scope, but CHANGE01 lengthens the window in which such state can exist. F2, low (contract refinement): the C13 recover paragraph in PAL-contracts-v5.md does not yet say how recovery settles cross-revision superseded/draining leases. The next C13 scope should require the same latest-intent settlement as CHANGE01 release, and should forbid treating admitted calls as ended without cessation evidence. F3, low (documentation): in PAL-contracts-v5.md section 5, the table row 'change | waiting_input/queued' says old questions are closed, while C02/C10 and the section 5 CHANGE01 paragraph use status superseded. The wording should be aligned. F4, low (advisory for PRI scope): TSK cannot enforce the provenance obligation (CHANGE01-SCOPE.md 'Closed API and authority' and 'Source-stop ordering correction'). If reused records are omitted, source-stop is bypassed for the new revision. PRI routing must bind change context_refs from the host snapshot plus model-selected sources. F5, informational: get_work for a superseded revision still returns its artifacts under current_artifact_refs (tasks_v5.py 301-313; test_artifact_and_verification_history_never_enter_new_current_set). This is acceptable because completion and VER check the revision, but consumers should not read the field name as meaning current. F6 (report process; affects verification only): input_sha256 could not be computed without tools (see evidence_limits).
next_dependency: Recommendation: implement scoped C13 restart recovery and the startup host lock before PRI host routing. The unmet contracts are as follows. Section 3 requires a startup lock that rejects a second process. C13 defines recover: it runs only at host start, confirms old-runner absence under the lock, reconciles through EXE.recover, invalidates running work, restores queued or waiting_input, preserves paused and cancelled, and never repeats completed operations. OWNER-EXCERPTS states that TaskStore has no restart-recovery method, and mock_runner_v5.py states that it has no persistent runner state or recovery. Without recovery, F1 means a single crash permanently blocks all task work, and CHANGE01's draining old lease and admitted-call conflict are exactly the states that would get stuck. PRI routing (the C01 submit/get_turn Turn ledger and PRI-02 targeting) is also unmet, but it should come second for three reasons: it would only add more ingress into a store that cannot recover; it requires evaluating real-model behavior; and its safety relies on the TSK fencing that recovery must preserve. Suggested smallest scope: a startup lock, plus a recover routine that (1) deactivates orphaned leases; (2) settles same- and cross-revision leases by latest intent (cancel, then pause, then queued, or waiting_input when an open question exists); (3) marks admitted calls whose cessation cannot be proven as unknown rather than returned; (4) keeps reservations consumed without refund; (5) abandons only owned started Steps; (6) preserves source-stop, grants, budgets and existing unknown states; and (7) does not adopt old-epoch VER results. It should use temporary SQLite and mock only, with no live DB migration. Two questions are technical decisions to record in that scope, not approval gates: whether death of the in-process mock under a held lock counts as cessation evidence, and whether EXE.recover must exist as a contract-shaped no-op when no operation capability was exercised (EXE source was not inspected). After that, scope PRI host routing: C01 and the change-proposal path with host-bound provenance per F4. Genuine human judgment is limited to: activating a real provider/UI path within the D-020/D032 cost and authorization bounds; the one whole-flow usefulness evaluation; any live DB migration or operational adoption; and publication approval under D045. Routine technical choices (lock primitive, recover ordering, test table, refinements F2/F3/F5) proceed autonomously within the existing decision lane.
